proof.criterion: Round-1 failure 1, now fixed. Spec: "two pods together cannot send more metadata traffic than one pod was allowed to" — the fleet's secret-store traffic must stay inside the four reads a second one pod alone was allowed.
proof.surface: Two cmd/broker binaries built from this head and started by hand on one Postgres database of their own, with BROKER_TRUSTED_PROXY_HEADER=X-Forwarded-For and a flood from a fresh source address on every call — the flood spread over addresses this bucket exists for — counting each process's own store reads from the refusal line the policy logs for a secret whose owner tag is gone.
proof.command: go build -o /tmp/hand/broker ./cmd/broker; two processes on one database; bash flood.sh 20 13381 13382 (one POST /v1/secrets/AUTO_READ_TOKEN/reread per pod per turn, each with its own X-Forwarded-For), then count the refusal lines in each pod's log
proof.observed: Each pod accepted 21 rereads in 20 s (1.05/s, the new per-pod cap) and each made 42 store reads — its own 21 plus the 21 its peer's fan-out drove — so the fleet read the store 84 times in 22 s = 3.82 a second, inside the 4.00 one pod alone was allowed. The same flood at the previous head measured 7.64. The bucket a caller meets is the new one: from one address, rereads 1 and 2 answer 200 and reread 3 answers 429 {"code":"RATE_LIMITED"} with Retry-After: 1. Started over the Google store (BROKER_SECRETS_STORE=gcp-secret-manager, its own prefix and KMS key name), the same binary answers 200, 200, then 429 with Retry-After: 4, which is GCPRereadOverallLimit's {Every: 4s, Burst: 2}.
proof.negativeControl: The red row that pins this, TestTwoBrokers/7, failed at the previous head with 'the fleet reads the store 8.00 times a second; one pod alone was allowed 4.00' and the same for the GCP bucket, and passes here unmodified; the hand-driven flood reproduces both numbers (7.64 then, 3.82 now) on real processes rather than in the row's arithmetic.

proof.criterion: Round-1 failure 2, now fixed. Spec: "A reread reaches every pod serving the same database" — including a pod that is draining, which is still being sent requests.
proof.surface: The same two hand-started cmd/broker binaries, the second given BROKER_DRAIN_SECONDS=20 and signalled, observed through its own HTTP answers and its own log.
proof.command: bash /tmp/hand/round2.sh — control with neither pod signalled, then kill -TERM on B followed by a retag of the fake store and POST /v1/secrets/AUTO_READ_TOKEN/reread at A alone
proof.observed: Control: A answered 200 and both pods read the store (+1 each). Signalled: B answered GET /healthz 503 and GET /v1/settings 200, so it was draining and still serving; A's reread 1.5 s into B's drain gave A +1 and B +1 store read, 2.21 s after B's SIGTERM, against B's five-minute reload. B went on answering /v1/settings 200 afterwards and exited 0 at 20.1 s, the whole of its drain. Shutting a broker down while its listener was mid-redial (its LISTEN backend terminated from psql, then SIGTERM at once with BROKER_DRAIN_SECONDS=0) exits 0 with no panic and no redial warning after 'broker shutting down', so endServing before st.Close holds.

Within this round the control is the unsignalled pair above: the same fixture and the same call with nobody signalled gives B +1.

proof.criterion: The implementer's further defect (a): a SIGTERM arriving between the bind and the end of boot must leave a pod that drains, not one that dies where its callers see a reset connection.
proof.surface: One real cmd/broker binary parked in exactly that window: a psql session of the test's own holds `oauth_provider_secret` in EXCLUSIVE mode, which blocks the `insert … on conflict do nothing` that oauthstore.Secret makes after the bind, so every boot stops there with the socket already bound.
proof.command: bash /tmp/hand/bootsignal.sh /tmp/hand/broker fixed — lock the table, start the broker, wait for 'broker listening', SIGTERM it, then release the lock
proof.observed: The broker logs 'broker listening' and stops; a caller reaching the bound socket while boot is parked is left waiting (curl exit 124 at its 2 s timeout) rather than reset. Two seconds after the SIGTERM the process is still alive. When the lock is released it finishes boot, logs 'broker draining drain=3s' and exits 0, 5.1 s after the signal.
proof.negativeControl: The same script against a binary built from the previous head with `go build -overlay` (cmd/broker/main.go replaced by its content at 3275c17cf765, the repository untouched): the process is DEAD two seconds after the SIGTERM, having logged `broker: fatal error="store OAuth provider secret: context canceled"`, and exits 1. So the behaviour comes from this change and not from the fixture.

proof.criterion: The implementer's further defect (b) and the shape the architect asked for deliberately: a pod reachable before it is on the reread channel, and — the harder half — a pod that cannot hold a LISTEN connection at all must still boot and serve, or a store outage becomes a broker outage.
proof.surface: Real cmd/broker processes on a fresh database, signed in as an ordinary Postgres role (a connection limit binds no superuser) whose limit is set to one, so the listener's own connection — the one it takes outside the pool — is refused while the pool itself works.
proof.command: bash /tmp/hand/listenfail.sh (control with the role uncapped, then `alter role … connection limit 1`), and bash /tmp/hand/bootrace.sh, ten boots each of this head and the previous one, reading pg_stat_activity for the channel's LISTEN session at the instant the process first answers a request
proof.observed: Capped: the broker bound in 0.23 s against the control's 0.24 s — a dial that fails answers the bind's wait as fast as one that succeeds — and answered /healthz 200, /v1/settings 200 and POST …/reread 200, with 0 LISTEN sessions established and one `broker: a Postgres listener has no connection; redialing … FATAL: too many connections for role` warning, and no 'binding before the reread listener has had an answer' line. So a database that will not carry the LISTEN costs this pod its fan-out and nothing else. Boot race: by the moment a pod first answers a request its LISTEN session is already on the channel, 10/10 at this head — and also 10/10 at the previous head, so the window this wait closes is between net.Listen and the dial, which a caller can only reach as an unanswered connection in the backlog; I could not make a reachable hole out of it either before or after.
proof.negativeControl: The uncapped control in the same script, on the same database and role: 1 LISTEN session established, 0 redial warnings, the same boot time. The only difference between the two runs is the role's connection limit.

notesForTheReviewer: Not a failure, but worth knowing: the bind's new wait closes the window between net.Listen and the reread listener's first dial. A caller cannot be answered in that window — the HTTP server has not started serving yet, so such a connection sits in the backlog — and ten boots at each head put the LISTEN session on the channel before the first answered request in every one, at this head and the previous one alike. The wait costs 0.01 s on a healthy boot and nothing at all on a failing dial, so it is cheap insurance rather than a proven fix.

A pod signalled mid-boot logs three sweeper lines at WARN — 'broker sweeper: expire pending requests error="context canceled"' and two more — because the sweeper legitimately runs on the signal's context and takes its first pass after that context has ended. Cosmetic, and the shape predates this change, but an operator alarming on broker WARN lines will see them on any pod killed during a deploy's first second.

The new burst of two is pinned by no test. Red row 7 holds the rate against the fleet's store budget and says nothing about the burst, and every api row now injects a bucket of its own, so a future change to Burst would be caught by nothing. The real binary answers 200, 200, 429 here, which is this round's evidence for it.
TestRereadIsRateLimitedPerAddress runs on the production broker-wide bucket and spends exactly two of its two tokens. One more reread in that row would be refused by the bucket the row is not about.
